storylines.label: Their Own
storylines.latest_title: Why founders keep failing to vibecode their own LLM inference engine

editorial.tldr: "Their Own" groups three items that share a phrase, not one developing event. They run from a Oct 14 paper on distilling web agents from black-box teachers to an Oct 21 study of models rewriting their own harness.
editorial.whats_new: A Startup Fortune piece on Oct 24 argues founders keep failing when they try to vibecode their own LLM inference engine; only the headline was available, so its evidence is unverified.
editorial.why_it_matters: All three touch the build-versus-depend question for agent stacks: distill a cheaper agent, let the model tune its own scaffold, or write your own serving layer. None yet gives production evidence.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not replace a maintained inference server (vLLM, SGLang or a hosted API) with a self-written engine on the strength of this piece; keep the existing stack until a source shows benchmarked results.

status.detail: Three unrelated items sharing a phrase; no single event is unfolding.

storylines.label: Reinforcement Learning
storylines.latest_title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide

editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has collected a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, and four Oct 20-22 arXiv papers on training tool-using and search agents.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 23: AWS publishes a hands-on guide to multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI, training on whole-task outcomes with a Wordle example.
editorial.why_it_matters: The SageMaker guide is the first managed-platform recipe in the thread, so teams on AWS can try outcome-based multi-turn RL without building the training harness. The arXiv papers cover rollout cost, stateful environments, search-state awareness and per-decision credit assignment; QwenGyre (a secondary-source report) and X-RIC remain research or telecom-specific.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using models, read the rollout-budget and twin-world credit-assignment papers for cheaper, finer-grained learning signal; if you run on AWS, try the SageMaker Wordle pipeline before planning around it, and wait for Qwen's primary QwenGyre release.

status.detail: A loose set of agentic-RL items; the newest moves from papers to a managed-platform guide.

storylines.label: Claude 5.5
storylines.latest_title: Kimi K3.1 Pro vs. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra

editorial.tldr: Latent Space's Oct 7 newsletter put Claude Haiku 5.5 ahead of GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing. On Oct 20, Google Cloud added Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to its Antigravity coding tool.
editorial.whats_new: R&D World compares Kimi K3.1 Pro against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra (Oct 23); only the headline is in the item, so the results are not confirmed here.
editorial.why_it_matters: Claude 5.5 models are reaching more surfaces (Antigravity), and a Chinese open-weight lab is now being benchmarked against Opus 5.5, so model-routing choices are being re-opened.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you route between models, rerun your own evals with Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3.1 Pro as candidates before changing defaults, and treat the Haiku 5.5 vs Luna claim as unverified until you test it.

status.detail: Claude 5.5 models are spreading to new platforms while Kimi K3.1 Pro is being compared against them; no outcome is confirmed in these items.

storylines.label: Kimi K3.1
storylines.latest_title: Kimi K3.1 Pro vs. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra

editorial.tldr: On Oct 16, coverage framed Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 as a name without a released model, and one report said a new Chinese export-license requirement for large AI models could affect it. A week later, reports said it was being readied for release after Arena testing.
editorial.whats_new: On Oct 23, TestingCatalog reported Kimi K3.1 is being prepared for release after Arena testing, and R&D World published a comparison of Kimi K3.1 Pro against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra.
editorial.why_it_matters: A pre-release open-weight candidate with a possible export-licensing hurdle is a planning risk: availability, hosting terms and timing are unconfirmed.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not wire Kimi K3.1 into production routing yet; queue an eval on your own tasks for when weights or an API appear, and check the license and hosting terms then.

status.detail: Kimi K3.1 appears to be nearing release after Arena testing, but the headlines here do not confirm a launch date or availability.

storylines.label: On-Policy Distillation
storylines.latest_title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation

editorial.tldr: Three arXiv papers from Oct 14–22 apply on-policy distillation (training a student on its own sampled trajectories, scored by a teacher) to different problems: machine translation, long-horizon coding agents, and the question of when the teacher should lead.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 22: an arXiv paper proposes advantage-based on-policy distillation, deciding per step when the student should follow the teacher.
editorial.why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is spreading from general post-training into narrow jobs (translation, coding agents), so teams distilling small models should compare it against SFT on their own trajectories.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you distill small models, run an on-policy versus SFT comparison on your own task trajectories before adopting either method; none of these papers has independent replication yet.

storylines.label: Large Language
storylines.latest_title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks

editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 6–21 items cover speculative-decoding security, knowledge-graph work, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, and materials extraction.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 22 adds a spectral-intervention paper, an empirical KG-to-text benchmark, and a Bashkir parameter-efficient adaptation suite; none extends earlier items.
editorial.why_it_matters: Treat this as a reading list, not a thread: the useful items for platform engineers are the speculative-decoding attack surface and code-translation hallucination mitigations.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run speculative decoding in production, read the Oct 6 security paper and check whether your draft model is an untrusted input; skip the rest unless it matches your domain.

storylines.label: Empirical Study
storylines.latest_title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks

editorial.tldr: Five unrelated arXiv papers share only the phrase "empirical study" in their titles; this is not one developing story. They span clinical-protocol coding agents (Oct 13), attack triage (Oct 21), UML hallucinations, Vietnamese classification, and KG-to-text (Oct 22).
editorial.whats_new: Oct 22 adds a UML-diagram hallucination taxonomy and a Vietnamese decision-model transfer study alongside the KG-to-text benchmark.
editorial.why_it_matters: No shared finding links these papers; the hallucination taxonomy for generated UML is the one most relevant to teams using LLMs for design artifacts.
editorial.take_for_builders: Skip unless a paper matches your domain; if you generate UML or design docs with an LLM, check the hallucination taxonomy against your own outputs.

storylines.label: Action Reasoning
storylines.latest_title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action

editorial.tldr: Three arXiv papers in three days examine the gap between LLM reasoning and acting. One proposes a benchmark for action and plan safety in embodied agents, and another tests frontier models on robot manipulation.
editorial.whats_new: A new arXiv paper formalizes the harness between an LLM and its tools as a Petri-net supervisory controller to block unsafe tool calls under prompt injection.
editorial.why_it_matters: These are research preprints, not products, but they point at where agent safety work is heading: checking actions at the execution layer rather than trusting the model's reasoning.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agents call tools, treat the execution layer as the place for enforcement; these preprints are unreplicated, so test any approach on your own tool set before relying on it.

storylines.label: DeepSeek DeepInfer
storylines.latest_title: Better Reasoning, Not Just Bigger Models: A Structure-Grounded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Inference

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek said on Oct 20 it is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the software that serves its production models. Coverage first framed it as a way to cut AI operating costs, then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic.
editorial.whats_new: Latent Space put numbers on DeepInfer on Oct 21: 155T tokens/day per cluster at roughly 80% margin and an 81-day payback, as reported by the newsletter.
editorial.why_it_matters: A production-proven open inference stack gives platform teams a reference for serving cost and throughput that vLLM-style deployments can be benchmarked against.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo and license before changing a serving stack; treat the margin figures as unverified until someone reproduces them on non-DeepSeek hardware.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; independent reproduction of the efficiency claims has not appeared yet.

storylines.label: DeepSeek China
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek Ban: China Threatens the U.S. With Countermeasures

editorial.tldr: Early October coverage framed DeepSeek as within about 3% of US rivals despite chip curbs, then a nearly five-hour outage on Oct 16 was tied to China's chip shortage. On Oct 19 the US ordered it removed from federal agencies.
editorial.whats_new: China threatened countermeasures on Oct 21 over the US federal DeepSeek ban, after Beijing publicly criticized it on Oct 20-21.
editorial.why_it_matters: Federal contractors and anyone selling into US agencies must now treat DeepSeek models and apps as prohibited in those environments, including hosted API calls; self-hosted open weights in private stacks are a separate legal question this coverage does not settle.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you sell into US federal customers, audit dependencies on DeepSeek APIs and fine-tuned derivatives now, and keep a swap-in model ready.

status.detail: DHS ordered removal across federal agencies; China has opposed the ban and threatened countermeasures.

storylines.label: DeepSeek Flash
storylines.latest_title: Latest open artifacts (#25): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, American-made models, and new regulatory controls in the US & China

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash first showed up in deployments: Dolphin's inference API went live Oct 11 and AMD MI355X posted AA-AgentPerf results Oct 14. Two OrcaRouter comparisons on Oct 16 then priced it against Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Step 5 Preview.
editorial.whats_new: DeepSeek shipped V4.1 Flash-1017 on Oct 17 with stronger coding and agent performance, lower inference cost and a first public search API; The Decoder says it beats larger rivals on agentic tasks.
editorial.why_it_matters: The update cuts per-task cost on agentic workloads and adds a first-party search API, so cost-per-task comparisons and search tool choices in agent stacks need rerunning.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your agent eval and cost-per-task numbers on Flash-1017 before switching, and test the search API against your current tool before replacing it.

status.detail: Flash-1017 is out; Harness v0.2.1-rc1 surfaced alongside an unannounced snapshot.

storylines.label: Google Antigravity
storylines.latest_title: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are now available in Google Antigravity

editorial.tldr: Google added local-model support to the Antigravity SDK on Oct 14, letting agent workflows run on a developer's machine and mix in cloud models. DeepMind then used Antigravity for Science on antimicrobial peptide search.
editorial.whats_new: Google Cloud made Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 available inside Antigravity on Oct 20, extending it beyond Google's own models.
editorial.why_it_matters: Antigravity now spans local, Gemini and Claude models in one agent harness, so model routing can live in the harness instead of per-vendor tooling.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you evaluate agent harnesses, rerun your coding evals on Antigravity with Claude selected and compare against local-model runs for cost and code privacy.

status.detail: Antigravity is widening from a Google-model agent tool to a multi-vendor, local-plus-cloud harness.
